title: Automated evaluation triggers for model pin and catalog upgrades
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Problem statement: When customers pin a model version or when the public catalog receives an upstream model upgrade, we currently lack a consistent, automated way to run regression evaluations against customer-specific prompt sets and Redwood canonical eval suites. That leads to silent quality regressions (or regressions discovered too late) and increases risk for customer-facing breakages.

Goal: Implement an automated evaluation trigger system that runs targeted evals whenever a model version is pinned by a customer or when a model variant in the Redwood catalog is upgraded. Triggers should be configurable (blocking vs advisory), support customer-pinned prompt sets and Redwood canonical evals, surface results in Console + Slack, and integrate with rollout/rollback policies.

Scope:
- Trigger sources: customer-initiated pin (Private/Dedicated/Hosted) and catalog model upgrade (Redwood-managed catalog changes).
- Eval targets: customer prompt sets (if provided), customer-provided reference prompts for sensitive customers, and Redwood canonical eval sets (accuracy, toxicity, instruction-following, latency-adjusted quality).
- Modes: dry-run/advisory (default) and optional blocking (for orgs that opt into pre-upgrade gating).
- Outcomes: Pass (no action), Advisory Alert (notify and log), Fail -> automatic rollback or create a canary hold and notify SRE/PM/Customer.

Non-goals: Full retraining, long running A/B experiments or external human labeling pipelines (we will surface links to those if configured).
acceptance_criteria: A trigger is created whenever a customer pins a model version in Console or via API and an eval job is queued automatically.
Catalog upgrades generate eval jobs for customers using that model in 'catalog-default' mode and for the Redwood canonical suite.
Evals can be scoped: Redwood canonical only, customer prompt set only, or combined; scoping is configurable per-organization and per-model.
Results are recorded in the Console rollout pane with per-metric diffs (score, latency, token-usage) and a pass/fail status.
Notifications are sent to configured channels (Slack, email) with a summary and links to detailed eval reports and replay logs.
For customers who opt into blocking mode, a failing eval prevents the model pin or blocks the catalog-version rollout and creates a rollback/hold ticket in Linear automatically.
Audit logs record who initiated the pin/upgrade, the eval config used, seed/version of eval harness, and timestamps for reproducibility.
Integration tests covering trigger creation, eval execution, result ingestion, and notification flows are added to the CI pipeline.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Arielle Chen: Draft spec created after CS flagged two regression incidents in Feb where catalog upgrades changed decoding defaults and decreased answer accuracy for a major customer. See incident notes: https://confluence.redwood/inci/INC-2026-02-decode-regression

2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez (ENG): Ran a spike to estimate cost. A full canonical eval run (10k prompts, multi-metric) on x1 GPU equivalents takes ~45m and $0.12 per 1k tokens; we should add sampling and prioritization to limit cost for large orgs.
2026-03-11 - UX (Maya Patel): Console needs a new 'Preflight evals' pane under Rollouts with a compact summary + expand for diffs. Prototype: https://drive.redwood/ux/preflight-evals-proto

2026-03-12 - Diego Martinez: Engineering proposal attached: use the existing Evals runner (optimize pipeline) + a lightweight trigger service that subscribes to model-catalog events and customer-pinning API events. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/908

2026-03-12 - Security (Nora Singh): Requesting security_review_required for customers who upload private prompt sets. We should ensure eval artifacts don't leak and honor org-level encryption keys. Marked: security_review_required = true in downstream checklist.
2026-03-12 - Arielle Chen: Decided on incremental rollout: start advisory-only for first two sprints, then gate blocking mode behind an explicit admin opt-in and completed security review.
2026-03-12 - Diego Martinez: Added dependency on 'eval-harness-2026' runtime upgrade (ENG-2207) to ensure reproducible eval seeds and deterministic tokenization across hosts.
